title: Encouraging More Contribution in Team Meetings
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Leaders shape meeting engagement by the behaviors they publicly recognize and reward. Six key behaviors unlock fuller team participation: asking good questions, respectful dissent, changed minds, specific recommendations, surfacing risks and tradeoffs, and evidence-based opinions. Leaders who intentionally praise team members for these actions amplify them across the team. What gets recognized by the leader gets amplified by the team, making deliberate recognition a high-leverage leadership practice.
points: Leaders shape meeting climate through the specific behaviors they publicly recognize and reward.
Publicly praising team members for good questions, dissent, and changed minds encourages others to contribute similarly.
Recognizing specific recommendations and risk-surfacing expands the range of contributions teams welcome.
Evidence-based opinions are a skill leaders can distinguish and reinforce to raise discussion quality.
quotes: When team members engage fully during team meetings, discussions are more robust, the full range of arguments and opinions find their way into the conversation, and decision quality goes up.
Leaders shape the climate of the room by the practices they embody.
What gets recognized by the leader gets amplified by the team.
Leaders who recognize team members for raising a concern encourage everyone to be more open and honest in their evaluations.” Archived from Admired Leadership on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
